# M0-c-05 — closing check after fix round 2 (lane `check/M0-c-05-close-r2`, flow flow-7, stage group 14, 2026-10-07)

Lane `check/M0-c-05-close-r2` ran under Opus 5.5 in Claude Code on the owner's Windows PC in WSL2 (Linux x64, Node
v24.12.0) on 2026-10-07, from about 04:39 to 05:52. The machine check printed
`wsl:Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-10900K CPU @ 3.70GHz:20cpu:16gib`. This seat is an implementer-side independent closing
checker. It is not the item's author (L-0293), its fixers (L-0305, L-0315) or its earlier checkers (L-0297, L-0307). Its
ledger row is L-0318. It changed no file of the item and ran no git command. It planned its probes and mutants before
reading the fixer's self-check lines. Its probes and mutants ran in its own mirror
`~/maps-scratch/waves/check-M0-c-05/r2/plat` (the item's six source files are `cmp`-identical to the tree). The
diagnostic copies `r2/diag` and `r2/diag2` carry a hook or a counterfactual in `legality.ts`, and nothing from them
reached `plat/`. Each mutant ran in its own copy under `r2/m/` with `--maxWorkers=1`, and each copy was deleted after.
No timing was taken or gated on.

## Verdict: FAIL — B-1 still fails on bent arterials; one new blocker (B-5, three survivors on C-0260 (1)'s stated limits)

| line | status | label |
|---|---|---|
| B-1 one-sided growth along an arterial | **still failing.** It is fixed on straight arterials. On a bent arterial, about 22 % of seed first steps are still rejected against the street across the arterial. | CONFIRMED |
| B-4 the rim's exact continuation | fixed (R07 is now killed) | CONFIRMED |
| B-5 (new) C-0260 (1)'s stated limits are not pinned | blocker. Mutants S07, S08 and S09 survive the full NEAR set, and each one changes fixture outputs. | CONFIRMED |

### B-1 — still failing: the far side is read from the start segment's line, so a bent arterial still grows one side

* **The mechanism.** `acrossOf` (`legality.ts:360–378`) counts a street as "across" only when both of its ends lie on
  the far side of the line through the arterial segment that holds the step's start (within 1 cm). The fixture's
  arterials bend, and their segments are 7 – 28 m long. Half a seed spacing back (about 80 m), the previous seed lies
  off that line, on the step's own side. Its street starts on the arterial and its first segment ends across it, yet the
  rule does not count it as across. The clearance (`legality.ts:601–614`) then rejects the step `parallel`, exactly as
  before the fix. C-0260 (1) declares only the opposite limit ("an arterial bending back … could let a step pass a street
  on its own side"). It does not declare this case.
* **Probe P1** (`r2/diag`, with a hook that logs each `steps === 0` verdict and the feature it cites). It ran the flat
  fixture through S5, at plain size and at 900 ha, on seeds 1 – 30 each. Every seed's first step from a through or
  primary was classified. **306 of 1 424 (plain) and 312 of 1 434 (900 ha) were rejected `parallel` for this one
  reason**, on all 60 runs. In each case the cited feature is the first segment (step 0) of a street that starts on the
  same arterial, with its end on the far side of the start segment's line and its start on the near side. **0** steps
  were rejected against a street wholly across a straight run, so the straight case is fixed. Only 15 and 16 steps were
  rejected against a street on the same side. Arterials holding at least two streets that grew on one side only:
  **32 of 213 and 34 of 210**.
* **Probe P1b, detail** (900 ha, seeds 8 and 10, stage 1). On seed 8, four of seven arterials grew on one side only:
  `way:0`, `way:4`, `way:10` and `way:12`, each with L 0 and R 3. On seed 10, `way:2`, `way:4`, `way:10` (L 0, R 3) and
  `way:8` (L 3, R 0) did the same. Every rejected other-side seed cites the previous seed's first street (`fst` i−1,
  `fstep` 0) at 71.5 – 80.0 m. That street's start lies 0.3 – 27.1 m off the start segment's line, on the step's side,
  and its end lies 1.1 – 34.8 m across. For example, seed 8 `way:0`: `sd [850, -3104]`, `d 7964`. This is the previous
  check's evidence pattern ("every rejection cites street i-1 on the same arterial … d 7551-7996"), now confined to bends.
* **The previous evidence re-run.** Seed 6 at 900 ha now grows L 13 and R 21 over all stages, with both sides on 7 of 7
  arterials. Seed 5 at 900 ha grows L 11 and R 16, with 16 bend rejections. Seed 10 at 900 ha grows **L 7 and R 19**,
  with 17 bend rejections and 4 of 7 arterials one-sided. The hand case at growthArea's spacing (`growth.test.ts`, *at
  growthArea's own spacing*) passes, but its arterial is a straight line along y = 0.
* **Counterfactual** (`r2/diag2`, the checker's copy only). In this copy, a street also counts as across when its first
  segment starts on the same way and ends across the start segment's line. On seeds 1 – 10, the first steps accepted
  rose from 342 to 441 (plain) and from 320 to 439 (900 ha). Bend rejections fell to 0. One-sided arterials fell from 9
  of 71 to 1 of 71, and from 16 of 70 to 1 of 71. So the residual comes from this one rule.
* **Required change.** Read "the far side" against the arterial, not against the line of its start segment. For
  example: a street whose start lies on the way the step leaves, and whose segment ends across it, is across. Or test the
  side against the way's polyline within the clearance. Amend C-0260 (1). Add a test that fails on the present code: a
  hand case whose arterial bends (for example 5 – 10° per seed spacing, built from short segments), seeded at
  growthArea's spacing with sides alternating, must grow streets on both sides at every seed. Then re-run the junction
  row and the 1 000-seed here-bar.

### B-4 — fixed (CONFIRMED)

* S01 (R07: the rim's `firstIndex` is the stage's live-way count) was **killed** by `capacity.test.ts` *the rim's
  streets continue the stage's acceptance index* (`1 failed | 11 passed`). S13 (`acceptedStreets(state, k) + 1`) was
  killed by the same test. The test asserts that the stage's prune removed streets and that the live count is not the
  accepted count, on seeds 4 and 5.

### B-5 (new) — C-0260 (1)'s stated limits are not pinned (S07, S08, S09 survive NEAR and change fixture outputs)

C-0260 (1) states three limits. A side test that is "within 1 cm, the lattice's rounding" (S07). "Every non-way feature
keep[s] the clearance as before" (S08). "A step leaving no way (any later step) … keep[s] the clearance as before"
(S09). The checker's probe P2 hashed S5's grown streets on the fixture (plain, 900 ha and small; seeds 1 – 10; 30 runs).
It ran on the base and on each mutant copy.

| id | mutation (`legality.ts`) | NEAR (14 files) | fixture outputs changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| S07 | the far-side tolerance 1 cm → 0 (`g.s * ea <= 0 && g.s * eb <= 0`) | **survived** 122/122 | 1 of 30 (plain seed 9: 39 → 38 streets) |
| S08 | the across skip applies to every feature kind (`if (across !== null && across(f))`) | **survived** 122/122 | 7 of 30 (for example plain seed 3: 44 → 50) |
| S09 | `acrossOf` reads the step's own street too (no `g.street === c.street` filter), so every later step that turns gets a far side | **survived** 122/122 | 25 of 30 (for example plain seed 5: 41 → 49) |

Each survivor changes outputs on honest inputs, so none is equivalent. *a street near the lattice rounding* places the
rounded start on the far side (y = 1), so the tolerance is never tested on the near side. *a step leaving no way* puts
no segment of the step's own street at its start, but every honest later step starts on its own previous segment.
**Required change.** Add tests that fail under S07 (a street's start rounded up to 1 cm onto the step's side is still
across), S08 (a band, shore, reservation or boundary segment wholly across the arterial still takes the clearance) and
S09 (a later step that starts on its own street's previous segment and turns reads no far side). These can be folded
into B-1's rework of `acrossOf`.

# M0-c-05 — closing check after fix round 1 (lane `check/M0-c-05-close-r1`, flow flow-7, stage group 14, 2026-10-07)

Lane `check/M0-c-05-close-r1` ran under Opus 5.5 in Claude Code on the owner's Windows PC in WSL2 (Linux x64, Node
v24.12.0) on 2026-10-07, from about 02:06 to 03:00. The machine check printed
`wsl:Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-10900K CPU @ 3.70GHz:20cpu:16gib`. This seat is an implementer-side independent closing
checker. It is not the item's author (`build/M0-c-05`, L-0293), its fixer (`build/M0-c-05-fix1`, L-0305) or its first
checker (`check/M0-c-05`, L-0297). Its ledger row is L-0307. It changed no file of the item and ran no git command. Its
probes and mutants ran in its own mirror `~/maps-scratch/waves/check-M0-c-05/r1/plat` (item files `cmp`-identical to
the tree; each mutant in its own copy under `r1/m/`, `--maxWorkers=1`, deleted after). No timing was taken or gated
on. The fixer's self-check lines were not used to plan the probes.

## Verdict: FAIL — B-1 still fails; one new blocker (B-4, a surviving mutant on B-2's promise)

| line | status | label |
|---|---|---|
| B-1 one-sided seeding | **still failing** — the seeds now alternate sides, but along each arterial only one side grows | CONFIRMED |
| B-2 the rim reuses lineage keys | fixed in the code | CONFIRMED |
| B-3 the growth-drift row | fixed | CONFIRMED |
| B-4 (new) B-2's pin does not hold the rim's first index | blocker (a surviving mutant on C-0258 (4)'s stated promise) | CONFIRMED |

### B-1 — still failing: the stagger is shorter than the clearance, so each run grows one side

* **Mechanism.** `growthArea` puts the seeds S/2 apart along a run, sides alternating (`proposals.ts:401–409`). S/2 is
  max(block depth, separation ÷ 2), and the clearance is that value plus half the secondary's width
  (`proposals.ts:182, 214`): 80 m against 83 m (walled CITY), 30 m against 33 m (ribbon). Every seed's proposal is
  popped at priority 0 in seed order, so all first steps are judged before any second step. A seed's first step runs
  parallel to the previous seed's first step on the other side of the arterial, about 80 m away, so `legal`'s clearance
  test (`legality.ts:557–571`) rejects it as `parallel`. The arterial lies between the two streets, so no thin strip is
  left. The next seed on the first side is 160 m from its sibling and grows. So the side of a run's first kept seed
  wins the whole run, and that side is set by the run's direction and its skips. This is the B-1 result that C-0258 (1)
  says it removed ("both sides grow in staggered T's; the run's direction sets only the stagger's phase").
* **Probe 1: isolation against the run** (`zz-r1/sides.test.ts`, stage 1). Judged alone against the standing features,
  the first steps of both sides are legal (seed 6, 900 ha: L 21/21 and R 22/22 `accept`). In the real growth, only one
  side's streets stand: seed 6 at 900 ha grew **L 1, R 22**; seed 10 grew L 3, R 19; seed 5 grew L 3, R 20; plain seed
  10 grew L 2, R 22.
* **Probe 2: the blocker found** (`zz-r1/sides2.test.ts`, seed 6 and seed 10 at 900 ha, the seeds' first steps in
  order). L was rejected `parallel` 20 times and accepted once (seed 6). Every rejected L step lists one feature inside
  the clearance and within 30° of parallel: the previous seed's R street on the same arterial, 75.5 – 80.0 m away. For
  example, seed 6 `i:1 way:0 … near [{street:0, otherSide:-1, d:7833}]` and `i:3 … d:7930`.
* **Probe 3: hand case at growthArea's own spacing** (`zz-r1/probe.test.ts`, 13 seeds S/2 apart, sides alternating, the
  real streams, seeds 1 – 8). `dense_core` grew **L 0, R 6** on 8 of 8 seeds (its first seed lies inside the band's
  clearance). `ribbon` grew **L 7, R 0** on 8 of 8 seeds.
* **Why the new tests stay green.** `growth.test.ts` *both sides of the arterial grow streets* hand-places three seeds
  200 m apart (`handCase`'s default `seeds`), not growthArea's S/2 stagger. `city.test.ts` *S5c's streets leave their
  arterials on both sides* counts sides over the whole map, where runs of either phase add up. On the plain fixture,
  seed 1 grew L 6 and R 17, so ≥ 1/5 passes. Mutant R03 (each seed's side taken from the count of seeds kept, not from
  its position n) also survives the whole NEAR set (115/115), so no test pins C-0258 (1)'s side-by-position rule.
* **Required change.** Make the seeds as built grow both sides of an arterial. For example, a street on the far side of
  the arterial it leaves is not a spine the step runs beside, because the arterial lies between them. Or the stagger
  across the arterial keeps at least the clearance. Choose one, amend C-0258 (1), and re-run the junction row and the
  1 000-seed here-bar. Add tests that are red on the present code: (a) S5c on growthArea's own seeds (or a hand case
  seeded at S/2, sides alternating) grows streets on **both sides of each arterial**; (b) each seed's side follows its
  position along the run, as declared (this kills R03).

### B-2 — fixed (CONFIRMED)

* **Probe** (`zz-r1/probe.test.ts`, seeds 1 – 10, 900 ha, S5 to stage 3, then `capacityStep` with demand = land per
  band × 2). The top-up `grown` ran on all 10 seeds with `dup: []` on all 10. The rim's indices start at or after the
  stage's accepted count: seed 4 accepted 4, rim [7, 9]; seed 5 accepted 4, rim [5, 6, 9, 10, 13]; seed 9 accepted 3,
  rim [3, 4, 5, 6, 9, 11]. `acceptedStreets` moves past the rim (seed 5: 14).
* **1 000-seed bar:** `dupKeys` = 0 on every seed (lineage keys of every S5c and rim street, per seed).
* **Mutants** R04 (growthArea drops `firstIndex`), R05 (the index ignores `firstIndex`), R06 (the tally forgets the
  first index) and R18 (`acceptedStreets` always 0) were all killed by `capacity.test.ts` *the rim's streets continue
  the stage's acceptance index*.

### B-3 — fixed (CONFIRMED)

* **The checker's 1 000-seed here-bar** (`zz-r1/barprobe.ts`, seeds 1 – 1 000, the item's `fixtureRun` and
  `metricDoc` with M0-k-05's METRICS, `--maxWorkers=8`, 1 482 s). Results: 1 000 rows, 0 errors, 0 per-seed misses.
  p5 min 47.3°; per-seed median 90.5 – 97.5°; 4-way share max 7.8 %; no turn cliff; S5c, the prune and S5d each once
  per stage; 0 top-ups; no batch refused; no work cut. Pooled: p5 75.1°, median 93.06°, 4-way share 1.06 %. The 167
  six-seed chunk medians run 92.0 – 94.4°. **Growth drift: 59 windows, p50 21.15°, p90 50.8°, 0 above 90°.** Read in
  arena order: 59 windows, p50 21.08°, 0 above 90°. All of this matches C-0258 (5)'s numbers.
* **The clause can fail.** `driftRow` asserts the > 90° clause at every size and the median from 20 windows.
  `bar-row.test.ts` kills R12 (the > 90° assertion removed) and R13 (the median floor raised to 1 000).
  `drift-grown.test.ts` (the hand pool, ≥ 100 windows, both clauses) kills R08 (no deflection limit) and R09 (limit
  × 2). The 1 000-seed reading above was measured on B-1's one-sided network, so B-1's fix must re-run it.

### B-4 (new) — the B-2 pin lets the rim start at the wrong index (surviving mutant R07)

* **Mutant R07** (`capacity.ts:357`): the rim's `firstIndex` is the count of the stage's *live* ways
  (`state.ways.filter(w => w.growthStage === k).length`, which counts S5b's primaries and the streets the prune kept)
  instead of `acceptedStreets(state, k)`. It **survives the whole NEAR set** (14 files, 115/115, 532 s). The test only
  asserts that the rim's first index is ≥ the stage's count, increasing and distinct. On seeds 4 and 5 the stage's S5b
  ways keep the live count above it. With no S5b way and a prune that removed streets, the live count falls below the
  accepted count, and the keys collide again (B-2's defect). C-0258 (4) promises that "the rim's streets take the
  stage's next lineage keys". R07 skips keys, so it is not equivalent.
* **Required change.** Pin the exact continuation. For example, assert that the rim's first accepted index equals
  `acceptedStreets(state, k)` taken before the top-up, or that `acceptedStreets` after the top-up equals that value
  plus the number of streets the rim accepted (the prune removes streets from the record). Use a case where the
  stage's prune removed streets.

## The blockers

### B-1 — one-sided seeding (the right proposal of every seed is dead on arrival)

* **Code.** `proposals.ts:550–553` makes each seed's two proposals in order, left (`base + π/2`) then right
  (`base − π/2`), both at priority 0. The left one is popped first and lays its first step from the seed point. When the
  right one pops, `legality.ts:419–424` ("the step leaves its start at ≥ the legal angle to every other way standing
  there") measures the unsigned *line* angle (`lineAngle`, [0, π/2]) between the right step and the left street's first
  segment. They are collinear, so the angle is 0 and the step is rejected `angle`. `deflectFrom` returns null because the
  start lies on that line (`side === 0`), so the rejection is final.
* **Probe (mechanism).** `zz-check/probe2.test.ts`: the same right step judged with and without the left street's first
  segment in the index → `{"withLeft":{"verdict":"reject","why":"angle","deflected":false},"withoutLeft":{"verdict":"accept","to":{"x":0,"y":-3000},…}}`.
* **Probe (effect).** Hand case (`handCase`, three seeds on a straight arterial), seeds 1 – 8, walled and ribbon: 16 of
  16 runs `"left":3,"right":0`. Flat fixture seeds 1 – 3 (`probe.test.ts`): stage 1 `"seeds":21,"left":21,"right":0`,
  `"seeds":21,…"right":0`, `"seeds":19,…"right":0`; stage 3 right 0 on all three.
* **Why a blocker.** C-0254 (3) declares "each with two proposals square to the arterial"; the code's result is one
  side only, on every seed and every arterial, with the side fixed by the arterial's run direction. That is an
  undeclared deviation from the item's own declared reading and a wrong result on an honest input, and fixing it later
  shifts every seed's output (a seed-to-output law, N-45: fix now). The here-bar's 4-way share is measured on this
  one-sided network: a seed that grew both sides would be a crossroads, so the fix must re-run the junction row.
* **Required change.** Make the behaviour and the declared reading agree: either the second side grows (for example
  its own seed position, or the sibling's first segment not counted against it at the shared start — the seat picks,
  the junction row re-run), or C-0254 (3) is amended to one proposal per seed with the side chosen by a stated rule that
  is not the arena's run direction. Either way add a test that fails on the present code, such as "on the hand case both
  sides of the arterial grow streets", or "the seed rule's side is the stated one".

### B-2 — the top-up's rim reuses the stage's lineage keys

* **Code.** `capacity.ts:356` grows the rim with `growthStep(state, k, streams, { boundary: grown, inner })`.
  `growthArea` gives it the same unit `growthStageLineage(key, k, reroll)` (`proposals.ts:426`), and the rim's fresh
  record numbers its streets from 0 (`index = rec.streets.length`, `proposals.ts:707–710`). So rim street *i* and the
  stage's street *i* hash to one lineage key.
* **Probe.** `zz-check/probe2.test.ts` (*top-up lineage collision*): S5 to stage 3 on the 900 ha CITY town, then
  `capacityStep(state, 3, …, { demand: land per band × 2 })` — the item's own top-up path, as `capacity.test.ts` drives
  it at × 1.3. Seed 4: `"dup":[{"rim":"way:55","rimIndex":1,"main":"way:53"}]`. Seed 5:
  `"dup":[{"rim":"way:68","rimIndex":3,"main":"way:63"}]`. Both ways of each pair stand after the prunes, in
  `state.ways` and in the arena.
* **Why a blocker.** §6.3 keys S5 ways by the growth stage in acceptance order, and the item lists that clause as a
  test. A lineage key is a locked-in identity (N-45: persisted or locked in, fix now). The top-up is a designed rung
  (F-BUDGET-STAGE) reached through the item's interface `capacityCheck(stage, demand)` / S5d's `demand`, and M0-x-05's
  rung fixture will take it.
* **Required change.** The rim continues the stage's acceptance index after every street the stage's growth accepted,
  pruned ones included, so no index is reused. Add a test on the top-up path (for example in `capacity.test.ts`)
  asserting that the lineage keys of the stage's streets and its rim's streets are distinct, and continue in acceptance
  order.

### B-3 — the growth-drift clause of the here-bar cannot fail, and misses at its stated size

* **Bar as built.** `growth-s5cd/bar.ts` `driftRow` asserts p50 15–30° and > 90° ≤ 1 % only when the chunk holds ≥ 20
  windows. Over the 1 000 seeds the largest six-seed chunk holds 4 windows. The item's four chunks hold 0, 1, 0 and 1
  (seeds 1 – 6: `[]`, 7 – 12: `[19.0]`, 13 – 18: `[]`, 19 – 24: `[99.4]`). The clause never asserts: a vacuous pass.
* **The bar at its stated size.** The exit bar is the growth-drift row "on 1 000 seeds … measured by M0-k-05's
  METRICS". The checker's 1 000-seed run, with the item's own `metricDoc` (S5c's streets `grown`, `organic`) and
  `growth.drift600m`, gives 165 windows on 162 seeds: p50 40.9° (quartiles 8.8 / 19.0 / 40.9 / 66.0 / 99.0 at
  p10 / 25 / 50 / 75 / 90), and 20 of 165 above 90° (12.1 %). The row's band is p50 15–30°, > 90° ≤ 1 %. Miss.
* **Where the turns come from (diagnosis, `zz-check/drift-diag.test.ts`).** The long streets with a > 90° window carry
  single vertex turns of 42–62° among the walk's ≤ 13° steps, which are legality deflections and bends: seed 23 way:17
  `…, 62.2, -10.1, 42.3, …`; seed 41 way:22 `…, -56.5, …`; seed 117 way:20 `…, 56.6, …`; seed 121 way:18
  `…, -57.7, …, -53.6, …`.
* **Why a blocker.** A bar that cannot fail on the promise it states, and the bar missed when run as stated. C-0254 (13)
  declares the chunks "descriptive below 20", but the row is about grown streets (§13.5 "net turn of grown streets over
  600 m"; §16 M0 (c)), and the listed 4 000-street test walks `headingStep` alone, without legality, so it does not
  stand in for the bar.
* **Required change.** (a) Assert the drift row over a pool that can fail — for example the windows of all the bar's
  seeds pooled, or a seed count chosen so that the windows exceed the floor. (b) Bring S5c's grown streets inside the
  row (p50 15–30°, > 90° ≤ 1 %): for example, a deflection that needs more turn than the class's curvature limit
  allows becomes a rejection, since §4.4 permits "deflected or rejected". Alternatively, if the row cannot be met with
  the designed legality, the miss is routed to the session as a bar decision with a choices row — never left
  descriptive.
